title: Constitutional Amendment 2: Prohibit a State Property Tax

context.text: Legislatively referred constitutional amendment, proposed as HOUSE JOINT RESOLUTION NO. 81 (113th) & SENATE JOINT RESOLUTION 1 (114th). Ballotpedia News reports the April 2025 final votes on SJR 1 were 26-5 in the Senate (March 26, 2025) and 89-6 in the House (April 21, 2025). Tennessee Lookout and WPLN report that Republican leaders launched a "Yes on 2" campaign in June 2026 with lawmakers, county officials, the Tennessee Chamber of Commerce and the Farm Bureau of Tennessee; Tennessee has not had a state property tax for more than 75 years. To pass, an amendment must receive more yes than no votes and a number of yes votes greater than one-half of all votes cast for governor, so a ballot that leaves the question blank does not count toward passage.

question.text: Shall Article II, Section 28 of the Constitution of the State of Tennessee be amended by deleting the following language from the first sentence: In accordance with the following provisions, all property real, personal or mixed shall be subject to taxation, but the Legislature and substituting instead the following: In accordance with the following provisions, all property real, personal, or mixed shall be subject to taxation, but the Legislature shall not levy, authorize, or otherwise permit any state tax upon such property, and the Legislature

summary.text: Attorney General's summary (as posted by the Secretary of State): This amendment adds text to Article II, section 28 of the Tennessee Constitution that prohibits the Legislature from imposing a State property tax on real, personal, or mixed property. WPLN News reports city and county property taxes would not be affected. The materials reviewed do not state a fiscal impact for the amendment.

measure.yesMeans: Adds language to Article II, Section 28 providing that the Legislature shall not levy, authorize or otherwise permit any state tax on real, personal or mixed property. (Secretary of State: a yes vote adopts the language in the proposed amendment.)
measure.noMeans: Keeps the current Article II, Section 28 language unchanged. (Secretary of State: a no vote keeps the current language in the Constitution.)

argumentsFor.text: Sen. Ferrell Haile (R-Gallatin), a regional chair of the "Yes on 2" campaign, told the Tennessee Lookout: "There may always be a temptation when things get tight not to reduce spending but to increase taxes, and I think the state should keep their hands off of people's property."

argumentsAgainst.text: Rep. John Ray Clemmons (D-Nashville), chairman of the House Democratic Caucus, said: "I wish Republicans would put as much effort into working with us Democrats to lower the cost of living for working Tennesseans as they put into amending the state Constitution."
